title: By Any Other Name, She's Still As Sweet

contact_edits.before: The production, by the star's wife, Donna Feore, gets off to a mystifying start with a small modern boy (played by their son) trying on a cadet's costume. As a framing device, it's unnecessary, and anyway never appears again. Once that's over, Mrs. Feore surrounds Mr. Feore with an excellent staging that gets the Festival platform swirling with action, as you might expect from an expert choreographer, but also fills it with intelligence. She shows you where to look and gives you things worth looking at and listening to. She only misreads one moment, when she has Wayne Best, otherwise admirable as the protagonist's friend Le Bret, shout his sympathy over Cyrano's rejection by the adored Roxane rather than confide it. Amanda Lisman, as the lady in question, simpers more than a bluestocking should, and their common enemy de Guiche is a more complex figure than the pantomime villain supplied by John Vickery. But there are some very nice small performances: Douglas E. Hughes as a drunken versifier; Robert Persichini doubling as a ham actor whom Cyrano drives from the stage and as the Gascons' commanding officer; Martha Farrell as a refreshment vendor whose adoration would strike Cyrano in a heap if only he could see beyond his nose. John Stead has arranged a fine duel and a great battle. Occasional passages are spoken in the original French, which may not be strictly logical, but is no less so than Shakespeare's anglophone Julius Caesar expiring with Latin on his lips. Besides, Burgess himself admitted that there could be no English translation for Cyrano's own dying word which is, and remains, panache. Which is also a fair summary of the whole show. - Cyrano de Bergerac is in repertory through Nov. 1. Call 1-800-567-1600 or visit stratfordfestival.cafor tickets and information.
